findings.summary: Acceptance verification is embedded in the live runner, preventing direct reuse of its provenance and publication checks.

assessment.reason: Maintainers cannot require or directly exercise the actual normalize, test-lifecycle and publication assertions without exiting through list mode or running a live model scenario. Changes to these high-consequence assertions therefore require reasoning through fixture/model orchestration, while offline suites exercise only lower-level helpers.
evidence: scripts/smoke_acceptance.rb:8-15 handles ARGV and exits or starts the live fixture at top level; requiring it is not a callable verification interface.
scripts/smoke_acceptance.rb:106-186 embeds normalize checkpoint/recovery, test A/B/C provenance and preservation assertions; lines 187-214 embed publication/readback/fixed-lease checks.
scripts/test_acceptance_support.rb and scripts/test_git_acceptance.rb require lower-level support modules rather than these actual driver assertions.
assessment.invariant: Extract only existing verification blocks behind explicit callable inputs while preserving their conditions, order, diagnostics, Git commands, approved-output mutations and current CLI/model/isolation behavior. Preserve all existing test scenarios/assertions; only scoped invariant guards may be added.

evidence: scripts/acceptance_support.rb now exposes verify_normalize!, verify_test_lifecycle! and verify_publication! with explicit keyword inputs; requiring support executes no client/workflow.

All three extracted verification bodies were compared by SHA-256 with their original driver blocks and are byte-for-byte identical. The driver retains CLI parsing, fixture/model setup, dispatch, guard ordering and the same 23 scenario names.

scripts/test_acceptance_oracles.rb directly exercises the actual extracted functions on synthetic inputs and owned temporary Git repositories: reviewed-prefix/private-proof rejection, independent recovery, approved-byte mutation, deferred/failed evidence, code-before-closure provenance, actual remote refs, paired readback, immutable expectations and missing-action leases.

Existing test bodies/assertions and live model/permission/budget behavior were preserved. Rake runs the new direct guards with the offline suite. No live model workflow scenarios were rerun; supplied unit traces do not certify workflow execution.

findings.summary: Invalid-ledger mutation subtests use unstable numerical labels instead of naming the rejected contract.

assessment.reason: A failing mutation=index diagnostic requires counting through positional mutation tables, and inserting a case renumbers later diagnostics. Descriptive labels make existing failures identifiable without changing protection.
evidence: scripts/test_ledger.py:266-287 builds invalid test-ledger mutations and reports subTest(mutation=index).
scripts/test_ledger.py:296-308 applies refactor mutations with the same numerical subtest label.
The original cases already isolate schema, identity, path, provenance, dependency, recurrence and closure rules; no new protected behavior is needed for this naming change.
assessment.invariant: Preserve every existing mutation, fixture value, assertion, test method/selector and evaluation order. Change only table/subtest labels; add no coverage or schema behavior.

decision.reason: Developer accepted the recommendation to leave R4 until these tests next need editing; descriptive labels offer a small diagnostic benefit, and no test changes are selected now.

evidence: The developer accepted the R2-R4 recommendation and explicitly allowed only R2/R3 edits plus recording R4's deferral.

The two mutation=index tables and all existing test inputs/assertions remain unchanged. scripts/test_ledger.py SHA-256 is 060f58bd5274107a00951cba4e3d710c73d9dfae3a5f85b1e1badafeb9d0de86 at the revalidated decision-context commit.
This is an actual contextual deferral: R4 remains open and held, with no closure or passing-test claim.

findings.summary: Normalize's local-handoff access rules are restated in runtime.md, rules/safety.md and rules/git.md, so every command that loads the runtime and rules reads the same exception more than once and each protocol change must be mirrored in three files.

assessment.reason: The protocol is summarized in runtime.md line 15 (1,296 characters), the Operational Helm state paragraph of rules/safety.md line 24 (972) and rules/git.md line 49 (752), while normalize-handoff.md already owns the full procedure; the three summaries were edited independently in this range, so a later change has to keep them aligned. The benefit is a smaller shared context and a single place to change. Copied rules must stay self-sufficient without the package, so the saving is limited.
evidence: prompts/shared/runtime.md:15 restates that only normalize registers locators, that ship and log/manifest discovery stay bounded and read-only, and the no-live-ledger limit.
rules/safety.md:24 restates the same registration, discovery and no-ledger limits for copied-rule sessions.
rules/git.md:49 restates registration and ship's cross-session discovery again.
prompts/shared/normalize-handoff.md is the authoritative procedure and already defines these boundaries.
assessment.invariant: Preserve every access boundary: only normalize registers locators, ship and review-anchor discovery stay read-only and bounded, no live-ledger access, and copied-rule sessions gain no locator or state access. Copied rules remain self-sufficient without the package.

findings.summary: Acceptance fixtures and oracles repeat the same Git invocation fragments: the fixture identity flags seven times and the changed-path listing five times.

assessment.reason: scripts/acceptance_cases.rb repeats the full -c user.name and -c user.email pair in five git calls and scripts/smoke_layout.rb in two; scripts/acceptance_support.rb repeats the diff-tree changed-path listing five times. A small private helper for each would give fixture identity and path listing a single definition, so a change cannot leave one copy behind.
evidence: scripts/acceptance_cases.rb lines 172, 191, 194, 196 and 197 pass identical identity flags.
scripts/acceptance_support.rb lines 154, 207, 208, 209 and 214 each build the same diff-tree --name-only listing.
scripts/test_acceptance_oracles.rb and scripts/test_git_acceptance.rb exercise these fixtures and oracles offline.
assessment.invariant: Preserve every fixture commit's author and committer identity, message and graph, and every oracle's exact path comparison and failure message; change only how the repeated arguments are written.

findings.summary: The publication oracle selects its no-publication behavior from a hard-coded list of four scenario names instead of a field on the scenario.

assessment.reason: verify_publication! at scripts/acceptance_support.rb line 256 branches on the scenario name, and that list grew from three to four names in this range when history-missing-handoff was added, while the scenario table already carries data fields such as missing_handoff and expected_updates. A forgotten name fails loudly rather than weakening the check, so the cost is a hidden coupling between two files, not silent loss of protection.
evidence: scripts/acceptance_support.rb:256 hard-codes history-remote-moved, history-missing-handoff, archive-completed-no-replay and ship-completed-backup-no-replay.
scripts/smoke_acceptance.rb previously held a three-name version of the same list before the oracle moved into acceptance_support.rb.
An unlisted no-publication scenario falls into the else branch and fails on the missing --force-with-lease check.
assessment.invariant: Preserve which scenarios forbid a git push and which require the fixed feature lease, and every raise message; change only where that distinction is declared.
